title_content.content: BP3177DG Deeply Dimmable Low PF LED Driver

paragraph_content.content: The BP3177DG is an isolated low PF dimmable LED driver, compatible with PWM or analog dimming signal, to provide high-precision and flicker-less light output. Dim to off function is available by PWM dimming signal.

The BP3177DG works in BCM and QR mode to improve system efficiency and EMI. BP3177DG adopts advanced primary-side constant current algorithm to provide excellent line and load regulation. Primary-side regulation also helps to eliminate second-side components and reduce system cost.
The BP3177DG provides with multiple protections to assure reliability of LED driver design.
The BP3177DG is packaged in DIP-7.
 Deep dimming depth down to 1%, compatible with PWM or analog dimming signal; support dim to off
 Tight LED current reference of ±3%
 Good current consistency in deep dimming
 Wide load voltage
 Built-in line and load regulation
 Multiple protections
 LED open and short protection
 CS short protection
 Over current protection
 Over temperature protection
 LED Ceiling Lights
LED Street Lamp

The BP3177DG is an isolated low PF dimmable LED driver controller, compatible with PWM or analog dimming signal, to provide high-precision and flicker-less light output.
After the system is powered up, VCC voltage will be charged to the turn-on threshold, and the controller begins to switch MOSFET. Output voltage will increase rapidly.
VCC pin is integrated with an internal clamping circuit to clamp VCC voltage. If VCC voltage is lower than UVLO threshold, the controller stops working.

BP3177DG adopts advanced primary side current sensing scheme. It can precisely control the LED current without secondary side sensing and feedback circuit. Quasiresonant peak current control is used and Flyback works in BCM mode to improve efficiency. Internal constant current algorithm of the BP3177DG guarantees highprecision output current, which can be set as:

The BP3177DG accepts analog signals from DIM pin to change LED current. For non-dimming applications, connector one capacitor to the DIM pin and leave PWM pin floating. The BP3177DG changes reference voltage to adjust output current. The maximum reference voltage from DIM pin is 1.8V.
The BP3177DG also can accept PWM signal for dimming. One ceramic capacitor should be connected from DIM pin to GND, to act as a filter.
If the PWM voltage is low for more than 18ms, the controller will stop switching. Once the PWM signal jumps to high (above 1.8V), the controller returns to switching the MOSFET.

When output is shorted, ZCD signal cannot be detected and turn-off time of the switch is extended to maximum to reduce power loss. When VCC voltage supplied by auxiliary winding is lower than VCC_UVLO, the controller enter into VCC UVLO protection.

The BP3177DG integrates with over temperature protection. If the junction temperature of the BP3177DG is higher than TREG, the output current will be decreased to limit output power and temperature rise. This function is helpful to improve reliability of system.
such as CS resistor open protection and CS pin short protection.
The following rules should be followed in the PCB layout of the BP3177DG:
1) The bypass capacitor of DIM pin and VCC pin should be placed close to the controller and GND pin as possible, especially the DIM pin, which must be close to the IC ground.
2) The resistor divider and filtering capacitor of FB pin should be close to the controller, and far away from the switching node, to avoid mis-triggering of OVP by system noise.

3) Trace of the current sensing resistor should be as wide as possible and kept close to GND for better output current sensing accuracy. Otherwise current regulation will be affected. Besides, GND of small signal should be connected to IC ground by
independent path.

4) The area of main current loop including area of primary side of transformer, MOSFET and snubber circuit, as well as the secondary current loop including the secondary side of transformer, freewheeling diode and output capacitor, should both be as small as possible to reduce EMI noise.
